answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce, non-transferable stake before it can submit jobs or vote on reputation updates. A dune of freshly minted accounts then cannot gain influence merely by multiplying names: each one ties up capital, and misconduct can forfeit that stake. A harbor operator can cap voting weight by the amount locked, while a kernel of honest agents checks claims against completed work. The defense raises the cost of a sybil attack, though it cannot stop a wealthy attacker outright.
